title: Patch an instruction and export the program
summary: Change an instruction in Ghidra's Listing without running the game, then export the program as an executable with your change, outside the game folder.

steps.title: Open the program in Ghidra
steps.text: In ANALYSIS: ANALYZE the game's executable once, then CONTINUE IN GHIDRA, and double-click the program in the project window.
steps.expect: The CodeBrowser with the Listing and the Decompiler.

steps.title: Go to the instruction
steps.text: Open Go To and type the address or a function name.
steps.expect: The Listing shows the instruction, highlighted.

steps.title: Patch it
steps.text: Context menu on the instruction, Patch Instruction; type the new instruction and press Enter. For raw bytes: Window, Bytes, switch editing on with the pencil button and type the hex.
steps.expect: The Listing shows the new instruction and the Decompiler follows it.

steps.title: Save the project
steps.text: File, Save keeps the change in Ghidra's project (beside the workspace); the executable itself is not written yet.
steps.expect: The program's tab loses its unsaved mark.

steps.title: Export the patched program
steps.text: File, Export Program, Format: Original File; choose an output file outside the game folder. Original File writes the program in its own format with your byte changes; C/C++ would write the decompiled source instead.
steps.expect: A summary dialog naming the file written.

steps.title: Run it from a copy
steps.text: Put the exported executable into a patched copy of the game (PATCHING, PATCHED COPY makes one) and start it there. The game folder stays as it was.
steps.expect: The game runs with your change; the original still runs unchanged.
